_genre_keywords_note: Ordered most-specific-first — the search returns on first match, so a compound subgenre (e.g. 'Deep House') must be listed before its generic parent ('House') or the parent's bare keyword swallows it. This is what the old dead 'genre_mappings' dict tried to express (mapping raw strings like 'deep house' to a canonical genre) but never actually wired into the code; removed in favor of just getting the ordering right here, one taxonomy instead of two disagreeing ones.
_pack_genre_overrides_note: Populated by researching (web search) artist/label/pack names that don't self-describe their genre in the folder name itself — e.g. a pack folder just named 'Deadmau5' has no genre keyword to match, but Deadmau5's real genre (progressive house/electro house) is a matter of public record. Keyed by exact source pack folder name (the same string _fallback_genre_from_pack would otherwise use verbatim); checked before falling back to the raw folder name. Add entries here instead of inventing a new genre_keywords entry when the giveaway is an artist/brand name, not a music-style word in the path.
_bpm_patterns_note: Ordered most-specific-first. The old first pattern had a bare '\D|$' fallback branch that matched ANY 2-3 digit number anywhere in a filename (track numbers, catalog codes) once the literal-'bpm' branches failed — validated against this library's real filenames, 2666 of 3534 matches (75%) were fabricated from unrelated numbers with no 'bpm' text nearby at all. Removed; the number-then-'bpm' pattern below now requires the actual marker producers use.
_key_patterns_note: The old 3rd pattern '(\w#?m?)(?:\s|_|$)' matched any single letter immediately before a space/underscore/end, with no word-boundary requirement — validated against this library, 100% of its real matches were garbage (e.g. picked 'D' out of 'BD Click.wav', 'A' out of 'ALPHA WET...'). Removed; bracket/underscore-delimited patterns are the reliable ones (30/30 correct in a random sample).
